# Results — Study 625 (Starting-Yield-Bond-Decade)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
10-year Treasury yield on the day you buy predicts your next decade of bond returns with R²
near 0.9; duration arithmetic, not forecasting** (Bogle's "Occam's razor" observation, Leibowitz's
rolling-yield convergence) — tested on Shiller's monthly GS10 series 1871→2023-09, extended to
2026-06 with the CBOE ^TNX index. Bond returns are a **constant-maturity 10-year par-bond
monthly roll** (Swinkels-2019-style simulation; method documented below). Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-07-03**; last complete month **2026-06** (the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `36732503ca4f`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Yield tape | Shiller "Long Interest Rate" (GS10, monthly average) 1871-01 → 2023-09 (1,833 months, staged GitHub-raw mirror), spliced with yfinance **^TNX** monthly-mean daily closes 2023-10 → 2026-06 (33 months) — **1,866 months** total |
| Return engine | constant-maturity 10y **nominal** total return: each month-end buy a par bond (annual coupon = that month's yield), sell one month later at the new yield with 9y11m remaining, collect 1/12 coupon; closed-form pricing, exact non-integer maturity |
| Forward decade | `fwd10` at month *t* = annualised TR-index return over the 120 months after end of month *t*; defined 1871-01 → 2016-06 (**1,746** overlapping windows) |
| Execution lag | **one, documented**: the signal is the month-*t* average yield; the position is entered at the **end of month *t*** (the decade starts strictly after the signal month) |
| Costs | long-only, one entry per decade: TreasuryDirect commission $0; ~2 bp one-way on-the-run spread → **0.20 bp/yr** amortised drag |
| Survivorship | none in the usual panel sense (single-asset national series) — but this is **one country's yield path** (the US never defaulted in-sample); a US-survivor caveat is named on the Signal axis |

## PRIMARY — non-overlapping decades (unit = decade, as in study 120)

15 independent decades, anchored on the first usable month (starts 1871-01, 1881-01, …,
2011-01). Plain OLS of the forward 10-year annualised nominal return on the starting yield:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| decades | **n = 15** (1871-01 … 2011-01) |
| **R²** | **0.923** |
| slope | **+1.086** (t = **+12.50**) |
| intercept | −0.34%/yr (t = −0.72) |
| identity test H₀: slope = 1 | t = **+0.99** — cannot reject the duration-arithmetic identity |
| MAE of the naive rule "decade return = starting yield" | **0.64 pp/yr** |
| residual std around the fit | 0.86 pp/yr |

The claim's number is on the tape: **R² = 0.92** on fully non-overlapping decades, slope
statistically indistinguishable from **1** and intercept from **0** — the fitted line *is* the
identity "you get what you paid for." The naive zero-parameter rule misses the realised decade
by only **0.64 pp/yr** on average.

## Phase sweep — the anchor month is not doing the work

The non-overlapping grid could start on any of 120 months. All 120 phases:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| R² min / median / max | **0.865 / 0.939 / 0.970** (120 phases, n = 14–15 decades each) |
| slope t min / median | **+8.75 / +13.89** |

The *worst* anchor still gives R² = 0.87 and t = 8.8.

## SECONDARY — overlapping monthly windows, HAC

All 1,746 overlapping windows share up to 119 months, so the OLS t there is fiction; the
Newey-West (Bartlett, **120 lags**) t is the honest secondary statistic:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n | 1,746 monthly windows |
| R² | 0.916 |
| slope | +1.140 |
| **HAC t (slope)** | **+32.71** |

## Sub-period robustness

| half | decades | R² | slope (t) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1871-01 … 1941-01 | n = 8 | **0.908** | +1.20 (t = +7.69) |
| 1943-10 … 2013-10 | n = 8 | **0.954** | +1.30 (t = +11.17) |

Both halves — gold-standard era and fiat era — carry the identity on their own.

## The 2020 cohort autopsy — the prediction was misery, and misery arrived

December 2020: GS10 average **0.93%**. The rule predicted a **0.93%/yr nominal decade** — the
worst starting hand in 150 years. **Partial decade, never pooled with the completed ones:**

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| starting yield (2020-12) | **0.93%** |
| realised so far (5.5 yr → 2026-06) | **−2.21%/yr** annualised |
| max drawdown en route | **−22.9%** (the 2022–2023 bond bear) |
| required over the remaining 4.5 yr to land the predicted 0.93%/yr | **+4.91%/yr** |

The 2022 crash did not break the rule — it is *how* the rule comes true: yields mean-reverting
up mid-decade produce capital losses first, higher reinvestment yields second, and the cohort
converges back toward its starting yield. The remaining-years requirement (+4.91%/yr) is
close to yields prevailing in 2026 — the identity is pulling the cohort home.

## THIRD AXIS — does the same trick work for stocks? **No.**

Same design, stock analogue: starting CAPE earnings yield (1/PE10) vs forward 10-year
annualised **nominal total return** of the S&P 500 (Shiller, monthly dividend reinvestment):

| quantity | bonds (GS10) | stocks (1/CAPE) |
|---|--:|--:|
| non-overlapping decades | n = 15 | n = 14 (1881-01 … 2011-01) |
| **R²** | **0.923** | **0.205** |
| slope (t) | +1.09 (**+12.50**) | +0.63 (**+1.76**) |
| MAE of "return = starting yield" | 0.64 pp/yr | **4.57 pp/yr** |
| overlapping HAC t (120 lags) | +32.71 | +3.48 (R² = 0.251, n = 1,590) |

For stocks the decade-unit t is **1.76 — below the bar**; the same arithmetic that locks a bond
decade leaves ~80% of a stock decade unexplained (the naive rule misses by 4.6 pp/yr — seven
times the bond error). The stock-side fix — netting the bond yield out of the earnings yield —
is [study 120's ECY](../../120-excess-cape-yield/README.md) (R² 0.70 on excess returns), a
*statistical* regularity, not an identity. **BUSTED.**

## Honesty check — the lock is NOMINAL only

Same regression with CPI-deflated returns (starting **nominal** yield vs forward 10y **real**
return): n = 15 decades, **R² = 0.239**, slope +0.81 (t = +2.02). The starting yield pins your
nominal decade, **not your purchasing power** — the 1940s and 1970s cohorts collected their
nominal coupons and lost in real terms. Named on the Tradability axis.

## Tradability arithmetic

One entry per decade in the deepest market on earth: TreasuryDirect commission $0; ~2 bp
one-way on-the-run spread → **0.20 bp/yr** amortised — **~319× smaller** than the 0.64 pp/yr
forecast MAE. Capacity: >$25T outstanding; long-only, no borrow. The "strategy" is simply
buying the bond: what the claim delivers is a **known nominal decade** (beta, not alpha).

## Synthetic control — machinery proof only, never market evidence

A seeded AR(1) yield path feeds the *same* pricing engine; `link` blends mechanical returns
with yield-independent noise. Nulls are **seed-averaged over 20 seeds** (single-seed nulls are
banned):

| planted link | mean R² | mean slope t | share \|t\| ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **1.0** (pure duration arithmetic) | **0.900** | +11.20 | 100% |
| 0.5 (half mechanics) | 0.729 | +6.65 | 95% |
| **0.0** (null — returns independent of yield) | **0.102** | **+0.20** | 10% |

The engine recovers the planted identity at full strength and does **not** manufacture it in
the null world (10% rejection ≈ nominal size at n = 14).

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** R² = **0.923**, slope t = **+12.50** on 15 non-overlapping decades
  (worst-phase R² 0.865, worst-phase t 8.75; HAC t = +32.71 on overlapping windows); slope
  indistinguishable from 1, intercept from 0. This is duration arithmetic showing up on the
  tape, robust in both centuries. Caveat: one country's (never-defaulted) yield path.
- **Tradability — INVESTABLE.** One purchase per decade, $0 commission at TreasuryDirect,
  0.20 bp/yr amortised spread, >$25T capacity. What you deploy is a **known nominal return**
  — beta, not alpha — and the lock is nominal only (real-return R² collapses to 0.24).
- **Works for stocks? — BUSTED.** Same design on 1/CAPE: R² 0.205, decade t = 1.76 (< 2),
  MAE 4.57 pp/yr. The arithmetic is bond-specific; the stock-side repair is
  [study 120's ECY](../../120-excess-cape-yield/README.md).
